decisions.summary: D1 states form/quality (Bassino & Ma Table 3) and market level for the c. 1745 Kyoto basket only; no block commits to each other era's form or market level where it differs (D3/D4 cells classify observed/reconstructed/borrowed, not form or wholesale/retail)
decisions.why: Q1 verbatim: 'for each basket good in Kyoto/Osaka c. 1745 (and where it differs, the other eras), what form and quality was it ... and were the prices the record cites wholesale ... or retail?'. Not impossible (SILENT with its search is always available), not implied elsewhere in the request, and the literal reading serves rather than defeats the purpose: Q4's Use averages each good across eras, which compares unlike goods if form or market level moved between eras. Fix: D1, or D3/D4's per-era table, states per era where the good's form or market level differs from 1745 (salt by the bale, cloth by the piece and so on), or SILENT with the search.

decisions.summary: D1: 'Siblings get a pointer where a good has a page (0261, 0273, 0279)', the Q1 findings themselves written only in 0249
decisions.why: FR-001 (accepted spec) places Q1 'in 0249 ... and its sibling pages where a good has one (0261 cloth, 0273 salt, 0279 charcoal)'; a bare pointer is thinner than the finding written there. Nothing makes the literal reading impossible or self-defeating, and the request does not imply it. Fix: the sibling pages carry their good's form and market-level finding, or the spec is amended through review to say a pointer.

decisions.summary: 0249 section per basket good: form and quality per Bassino & Ma's note, market level per price (Mitsui 'retail' as editor's label, Osaka 1757 soybean wholesale, constructs at no level), Mitsui miso/soy sauce as observed alternatives, markups SILENT for Kyoto/Osaka 1745 with ATTESTED ONLY FOR cases, fish eaten SILENT
decisions.why: Answers Q1's figure needed for c. 1745 (form/quality, wholesale or retail, markup where found) under FR-001; the SILENT and ATTESTED ONLY FOR outcomes are findings, not scope choices.

decisions.summary: 0265: Osaka Mitsui rents 1814/1846, Edo back-lot rents, a 9-shaku x 2-ken room as labeled project arithmetic; Kyoto and c. 1745 SILENT with leads named and to the download list
decisions.why: Q3's historical rent with room size, nearest to c. 1745 as the question allows ('or the nearest'); FR-001 places it in 0265; FR-004 covers download-list leads.

decisions.summary: New question beside 0286: per Japanese era a table of soybeans, fish, cloth, salt, fuel, housing, each cell observed/reconstructed/borrowed (with the era borrowed from)/held unused/absent, prices in 0286's format; 0286's Kyoto salt line revised to the unit change; fish SILENT
decisions.why: Q4 and gm-assistant's addendum (which era each reconstructed price was borrowed from), FR-001; the salt revision corrects an existing per-era observed/reconstructed claim and D8 routes it through escalation-check.

decisions.summary: New question beside 0288 in the same shape for Chinese eras; official and market prices kept apart; beijing-1500 SILENT; held-but-unused prices named
decisions.why: Q4 'China beside it', FR-001.

decisions.summary: New money question in Money and prices: what baskets compute, index choice (Laspeyres/Paasche/Fisher, spread as uncertainty), one figure or several, which papers put a basket into modern money (Allen 2017, Moatsos), rice as numeraire with weaknesses, poverty-line housing allowance; derived rules labeled
decisions.why: Q5 in full plus Q3's poverty-line candidate, placed and tagged per FR-002a; absence of a named geometric-mean finding is an outcome of the search, not a scope choice.

decisions.summary: New question(s) in Comparative money: modern US like-for-like product per good at retail (snapshot rule) and at wholesale where historical is wholesale, dated with link; housing candidates per m2-year; US adult yearly quantities; never sets a Rokugani price; snapshot never edited
decisions.why: Q2, Q3 modern candidates, Q6 under FR-002; 'nearest product with what differs' is the honest exit, not a narrowing. Note: Q3 asks for each candidate 'what each measures' - D6 should carry that when written, but nothing in the block excludes it.

decisions.summary: 0249 a section per basket good: form/quality per Bassino & Ma Table 3, market level per price, Mitsui miso/shoyu as observed alternatives, markups SILENT/ATTESTED ONLY FOR, fish eaten SILENT; siblings 0261/0273/0279 carry their own good's finding; other eras delegated to D3/D4 tables.
decisions.why: Covers Q1's per-good form, quality, wholesale/retail and markup for c. 1745, and the round-1 sibling finding (FR-001 'where a good has one') is fixed. Its other-eras clause is only as good as D3/D4's column set; that gap is ruled under D3-columns, not here.

decisions.summary: 0265: Osaka Mitsui rents 1814/1846, Edo back-lot rents, labeled arithmetic for a 9x2 room, Kyoto and c. 1745 SILENT with leads named.
decisions.why: Answers Q3's historical rent with room size, or SILENT with the search, as asked.

decisions.summary: D3 (and D4 'in the same shape') defines the per-era table as soybeans, fish, cloth, salt, fuel and housing only; D1 now routes Q1's other-eras form/market level for every basket good into those cells.
decisions.why: New in round 2, created by the fix: D1 now delegates Q1's '(and where it differs, the other eras)' for EACH basket good to D3/D4's cells, but rice, barley/wheat, buckwheat/millets, beans and the oils have no column there. Q4's second clause asks 'per era, which of ITS goods are observed and which are reconstructed or borrowed' and its Figure needed is 'a per-era list of observed vs reconstructed goods', unqualified; the six are the GM-side list only for Q4's first question. The addendum names beans, buckwheat/millets and barley (three not columns) and asks the list to say where each was borrowed from. D3's parenthetical naming kyoto-1745's beans and grains assumes cells the table definition does not give. Not impossible, not implied by the request, and it defeats the addendum's purpose (no double-counting when averaging every good). Fix: D3 says the per-era table carries every good the era prices - rice, the grains, beans and the oils as columns beside Q4's six - each cell with its observed/reconstructed/borrowed-from status and its form and market level where they differ from 1745; D4 inherits by 'same shape'.

decisions.summary: New question beside 0286, cells observed/reconstructed/borrowed-from/held-unused/absent, new prices in 0286 format, Kyoto salt bale revision, Edo-period fish SILENT, per-cell form and market level where different from 1745.
decisions.why: Q4's figures and gm-assistant's addendum (borrowed-from), plus Q1's other eras for the goods it holds; FR-001's placement.

decisions.summary: New question beside 0288 in D3's shape: Timkovski 1821 Peking, Changzhou cloth ATTESTED ONLY FOR, Beijing fish as secondary reports, official/market kept apart, per-cell form/market level vs 1745, beijing-1500 SILENT.
decisions.why: Q4's 'China beside it' and Q1's other eras; its column set inherits D3's and is covered by the D3-columns ruling.

decisions.summary: New money question: what baskets compute, index choice (Fisher, spread as uncertainty), one figure or several, which papers put a basket into modern money, rice as numeraire with weaknesses, poverty-line housing allowance; derived rules labeled.
decisions.why: Q5 clause by clause and Q3's poverty-line allowance, placed and tagged as FR-002a requires.

decisions.summary: Comparative question(s): per good the like-for-like US product at retail and at wholesale where the historical price is wholesale, dated with links; housing candidates per m2-year with what each measures; US adult yearly quantities; never sets a Rokugani price; snapshot never edited.
decisions.why: Q2, Q3's modern candidates (now with 'what each measures', its Figure needed) and Q6; FR-002; 'never edited, a corrected one is a new snapshot' is the request's own words.
